column1: # Recipe parity ledger — the ratchet that makes partial kernel coverage an honest number.
# All 96 operation names implemented by massing's authoring service, extracted verbatim and in order from
# RECIPES in services/data/src/aec_data/edit.py @ ibuilder/massing. The order is the source file's order, not
# alphabetical, so re-extracting produces a reviewable diff rather than a reshuffle.
# Why this file exists rather than a number in a README: a kernel that supports 15 of 96 operations is fine and
# expected (see docs/adr/0001-two-kernels.md), but a kernel that is *vague* about which 15 is not. Every gap
# here is a control the ribbon dims with a specific reason instead of hiding. The count can only go up, and
# scripts/check-recipe-parity.mjs enforces that against the committed floor.
# Status vocabulary — and the distinction between the first two is the whole point:
#   yes      implemented AND verified live by @massingviewer/kernel-conformance. Not a claim; a passing test.
#   planned  intended for this kernel, not yet implemented. Returns `unsupported` today, honestly.
#   no       deliberately out of scope for this kernel. Not a TODO.
# Columns are one per kernel so a single grep answers "what can I do offline?" — the question a user actually
# has, and the one that decides whether they need a server at all.
